title: Linear-moving Anthrobots are more bilaterally symmetric about their movement axis

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Linear-moving Anthrobots are more bilaterally symmetric about their movement axis

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Linear-moving Anthrobots show higher bilateral symmetry of cilia distribution about their axis of movement than circular movers; for circular bots, but not linear bots, the 90-degree rotated axis is more symmetric than the movement axis (p = 0.048), supporting distinct local symmetry profiles for distinct movement types.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: Motile Living Biobots Self-Construct from Adult Human Somatic Progenitor Seed Cells

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Gumuskaya G 2024, Motile Living Biobots Self-Construct from Adult Human Somatic Progenitor Seed Cells › Results › Anthrobots Show Bilateral Asymmetry Along Movement Axis

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: Taken together, these findings support our hypothesis that Anthrobots with distinct movement types have distinct local bilateral symmetry profiles, with linear bots showing higher bilateral symmetry.

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Gumuskaya G, Srivastava P, Cooper BG, Lesser H, Semegran B, Garnier S, Levin M, “Motile Living Biobots Self-Construct from Adult Human Somatic Progenitor Seed Cells”, Advanced science (Weinheim, Baden-Wurttemberg, Germany) (2024), doi:10.1002/advs.202303575; section “Results › Anthrobots Show Bilateral Asymmetry Along Movement Axis”. Scope: 28 displacing NHBE-derived Anthrobots (15 circular, 13 linear)

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2024-anthrobots-16: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.68

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The symmetry measures and comparison axes are explicit and can be checked with standard image analysis. Public summaries permit partial verification, but the small sample and borderline p-value limit generality.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Recompute cilia bilateral-symmetry indices along movement and rotated axes for the 13 linear and 15 circular bots and reproduce paired tests with effect sizes.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
The sample is only 28 bots.

Axis selection and multiple symmetry metrics create analytic flexibility.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
discriminating power: 0.72
operationalizability: 0.95
data adequacy: 0.38
data existence: 0.6
analysis feasibility: 0.8

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Symmetry about the movement axis versus a rotated axis is a concrete paired comparison, which is what the paper reports. The cilia coordinates for those 28 bots were not released. The contrast is informative in design and impossible to rerun until the points or a new paired sample exist.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: For each linear and circular bot, compute bilateral cilia symmetry about the movement axis and about the axis rotated 90 degrees, then repeat the paired rank test. Higher movement-axis symmetry in linear bots, and the opposite pattern in circular bots, would support distinct symmetry profiles; no axis difference would refute it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
The test uses 15 circular and 13 linear bots, and the coordinates are not public.

The movement axis is taken from tracking, so symmetry and behavior are not independent measurements.

A reported p-value near 0.05 cannot be checked for leverage points without the pairs.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
data existence: 0.14
data adequacy: 0.18
analysis feasibility: 0.18
operationalizability: 0.84
discriminating power: 0.5
